_comment: Saltbound hub ship, design data (generated from Docs/Design/HubShip/hub_data.js; do not edit, change hub_data.js and run Tools/design/render_hub_ship.py --data).

frame.x: forward from the stern (0) to the stem (160)
frame.unreal: cm; +X forward, +Y starboard, +Z up; the ship actor pivot at x 80, y 0, z 0: X_cm = (x - 80) * 100, Y_cm = y * 100, Z_cm = z * 100
frame.face: degrees in plan: 0 = towards the bow (+x), 90 = to starboard (+y); equals Unreal yaw in the ship frame

open.name: The Keelgate
open.sub: chamber at the foot of the Well

locked.name: Sterncastle
locked.sees: Tall doors at the aft end of the main deck, barred from inside. The stern windows glow at night; the great wheel on the quarterdeck is lashed and never turns.

locked.name: Stern quarters
locked.sees: Doors off the Water Hall’s aft quay, and the aft galleries over the water with their shutters.

locked.name: Stern stores
locked.sees: Shuttered bays along the Water Hall’s aft quay.

locked.name: Timber store
locked.sees: Iron grilles on the port side of the Slip; stacked timber behind them.

locked.name: Keel Walk
locked.sees: A heavy door in the Slip’s forward wall and another in the Keelgate chamber: the first shortcut to open.

locked.name: The Holds
locked.sees: Iron grilles in the Keelgate chamber’s forward wall; padlocked cargo hatches on the main deck.

locked.name: Purser’s stores
locked.sees: A door in the Tally House’s forward wall, by the pay booth.

locked.name: The Ropewalk
locked.sees: Double doors off the Well’s port gallery; the creak of a rope being laid.

locked.name: Mess and galley
locked.sees: A door off the Well’s forward gallery; the galley chimney smokes on the main deck.

locked.name: Guild rooms
locked.sees: Doors with painted crests off the Well’s aft gallery; their galleries over the Water Hall’s forward quay.

locked.name: Lantern Market
locked.sees: A rope across the forward gallery with a board: “Market closed”; light and voices behind shutters.

locked.name: Archive
locked.sees: A door with a brass plate off the Well’s aft gallery; its galleries high over the Water Hall.

locked.name: Inn and bunkrooms
locked.sees: A door off the forward gallery; laughter behind it in the evening.

locked.name: Forecastle and bow
locked.sees: Chained ladders and closed doors at the forward end of the main deck; the bowsprit beyond.

locked.name: Cargo deck
locked.sees: The forward end of the main deck behind a rope and a board (“Cargo work, keep clear”): lashed cargo under nets, the padlocked hatches, the ship’s boats.

locked.name: Masts and tops
locked.sees: Shrouds whose ratlines start out of reach; the tops’ lanterns at night.

locked.name: The Deep
locked.sees: The Keelgate: the ancient seal in the floor at the foot of the Well, faintly lit from inside.

locked.name: Sail lofts and workshops
locked.sees: Doors off the Well’s gun-deck gallery; canvas and tar.

G1.name: Barred door
G1.why: Somebody’s room or business, not open to you yet.
G1.how: A timber door with an iron bar and a padlock. E: a short line of why.

G2.name: Rope and board
G2.why: Work going on, or closed for now.
G2.how: A rope across the way on stanchions (or between the door posts), a hand-painted board on it.

G3.name: Chained ladder or hatch
G3.why: Up or down: masts, forecastle, cargo hatches.
G3.how: A chain through the rungs or the grating, padlocked.

G4.name: Shutters
G4.why: Windows and bays of locked rooms.
G4.how: Closed shutters: nothing inside to see, nothing inside to build.

G5.name: Ancient seal
G5.why: The lost civilisation: the main quest.
G5.how: Pale seamless stone, turquoise lines, no handle, no lock.

G6.name: Iron grille
G6.how: Bars you see through into a shallow set, 2 to 3 m deep, and no further.
G6.line: Stacked timber, and no way in.

outside.hull_section: Planked all the way down (D64: no pale ancient band outside; the ancient hull shows only inside, at the Keelgate and the Deep): flat bottom +/-6 m at the keel (z -12), +/-16 m at z -6, +/-19 m at the waterline, widest +/-20 m at z +6, tumblehome to +/-18.8 m at the main deck rail and +/-17.4 m at the taffrail. Fine at the ends below the water (hub.form): the run aft narrows to the sternpost, the entry forward is finer than the deck outline.
outside.stern: A galleon’s stern (D64): the sterncastle rises in two tiers, the quarterdeck over x 24..48 (deck 22.5) and the poop over x 0..24 (three storeys, deck 28.5). Below the counter (z 8.5) the hull narrows to the sternpost and the one rudder; above it the stern is full width, round in plan (its corners 2.6 m forward of its middle) and leans aft a little. On its face: rows of tall cabin windows on each storey, open stern galleries with balustrades at sc1 and sc2 running round the corners into the quarter galleries (x 2..13, standing out 2.6 m, three storeys, domed), the name in carved brass letters under the taffrail, three great lanterns on the taffrail. The tiller comes in through the counter; the lashed great wheel is on the quarterdeck.
outside.sides: Dark tarred planking in strakes about 0.55 m wide with a lively sheer (hub.sheer: up 2.2 m at the stern, 2.6 m at the stem); heavy wales in a belt at the waterline and at the deck lines, standing out like mouldings; ochre bands; lidded square ports (1 m) on every deck below the main deck down to the dock deck, cream-framed windows above it; most shut, some lit at night. Channels with deadeyes at each mast. The hidden doors at x 32..40 on both sides, from under the water to 13 m: shut, the planking, wales and painted port lids run on across them; only a seam and the iron hinge straps show.
outside.masts: x 68, 100, 140 (hub.rig in numbers); 54, 76, 64 m above the main deck; the mizzen’s lowest yard a lateen yard; every sail furled on its yard; shrouds to the channels, stays forward, a long oxblood-and-cream pennant at the main truck.
outside.bow: Forecastle x 134..160, a storey over the main deck with a rail; a plain stem with two hawse holes and their cables to the anchors ahead; the beakhead out from the stem under the bowsprit (a grated platform, headrails curving up to the forecastle, a carved figurehead); the bowsprit from (154, 23.5) to (188, 30.5) with its spritsail yard, held down by its bobstay.
outside.colours: Hull planking dark tarred brown; ochre bands, muted; window frames cream; carvings and the name brass, muted; decks teak and its light and dark variants; canvas; iron.
